items.title: Google Search Profiles: Publisher Profile Pages Officially Live
items.summary: After tons and tons of testing and tweaking, Google is officially announcing what it calls Search profiles and what I called Discover publisher pages.  Google said Search profiles provide "a central place to showcase their latest articles, videos and social posts."

items.title: Microsoft Advertising To Update UTM Analytics Auto-Tagging Sep. 2
items.summary: Microsoft emailed advertisers notifying them that Microsoft Advertising will update UTM auto-tagging beginning on September 2, 2026. Microsoft added that no action is required on your part, as the updated tags will be applied automatically.

items.title: Coming Soon: Connecting Google Business Profile To Google Analytics
items.summary: Google will soon allow you to connect your Google Business Profile with Google Analytics.  Google sent out an email to some businesses saying this is coming soon, within the next "few weeks."

items.title: Google Passkey & Security Agent Added To Account Security and Safety Doc
items.summary: With the rise of Google Ads accounts being hijacked, Google has updated its Account security and safety help document with more details on passkeys and the security agent feature. This is in addition to a number of changes Google made recently around ad account security.

items.title: Google Dialog: Does This Business Offer Rewards In Exchange For Reviews
items.summary: About five months ago (I missed it), Google began asking searchers if the business location they are visited offers rewards in exchange for reviews. The prompt that comes up in the app asks, "Does this business offer rewards in exchange for reviews?"

items.title: AI Citation drift: How stable are sources in AI search results?
items.summary:
A source cited in an AI response today may well have disappeared by next week. Our analysis of 82,619 prompts over 17 weeks shows that Google replaces 56% of sources in AI-generated responses every week, whilst ChatGPT replaces as much as 74%. In this article, we will explain who stays, […] 
 Der Beitrag  AI Citation drift: How stable are sources in AI search results?  erschien zuerst auf  SISTRIX .
